items.title: The old-price slide
items.setting: After a client presentation at a workplace
items.contrast: A shared self-own about a recoverable mistake versus a competence wound that needs reassurance.
items.cost_of_misread: If B laughs at the second reading, A hears that her panic about looking careless is entertaining. If B treats the first as a crisis, B makes a finished mishap tense and embarrassing.

version_1.label: Recovered blunder as a story
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's chuckle offers the error as a harmless anecdote, and B's laugh joins the release.
version_1.correct_next_move: Laugh along briefly, then trade a similar work-story or move on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I showed the client the old-price slide [chuckles].

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But Maya caught it before they signed [laughs].

version_2.label: Still ashamed of the blunder
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh is cover for feeling incompetent; B's gentle delivery treats the recovery as reassurance, not a punchline.
version_2.correct_next_move: Reassure A that the mistake was caught and avoid making her the office joke.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I showed the client the old-price slide [nervous laugh].

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But Maya caught it before they signed [gentle].

items.title: The follow-up scan
items.setting: At home after a medical appointment
items.contrast: Darkly comic frustration with medical bureaucracy versus fear that needs practical care.
items.cost_of_misread: Reading fear as a bit invites jokes about a genuinely frightening health concern. Reading the comic version as catastrophe can make A more alarmed than they were.

version_1.label: Bureaucracy as shared absurdity
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A uses a small chuckle to invite B into frustration with the endless appointments, not to ask for rescue.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the mild complaint and stay calm rather than escalating the medical meaning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: They want me back for one more scan [chuckles].

version_2.label: Scared behind a laugh
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh covers real dread; B's gentle answer signals that the waiting is not being treated as amusing.
version_2.correct_next_move: Offer company, ask what A needs, and do not make the scan into a joke.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: They want me back for one more scan [nervous laugh].

items.title: The liquid birthday cake
items.contrast: Affectionate teasing over a cooking flop versus hurt at being embarrassed during a celebration.
items.cost_of_misread: If B piles onto the second reading, B turns A's hurt into public mockery. If B over-apologizes to the first, B kills a family joke A was inviting.

version_1.label: A family cooking joke
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laughs frame the underbaked cake as a ridiculous shared memory.
version_1.correct_next_move: Tease lightly, let A tease back, and keep the joke warm.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You served the cake with the center still liquid [laughs].

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is not what the recipe said [chuckles].

version_2.label: An embarrassment that still stings
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's strained laugh tries to contain hurt; B's soft delivery recognizes that this is not permission to keep joking.
version_2.correct_next_move: Apologize for the embarrassment and stop defending the mistake as funny.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You served the cake with the center still liquid [strained].

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is not what the recipe said [strained].

items.title: The team-lead announcement
items.relationship: Two coworkers who know each other well
items.contrast: Genuine good news received with delighted disbelief versus a hollow title received with bitter irony.
items.cost_of_misread: Consoling the first reading punctures a real achievement. Giving full-throated congratulations to the second can sound like agreement that A should be grateful for a bad deal.

version_1.label: Happy disbelief
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's laugh is delighted disbelief at being chosen, and B's response celebrates the news.
version_1.correct_next_move: Congratulate A and ask what the new role will involve.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: They picked me for team lead [laughs].

version_2.label: A title A does not want
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's dry laugh makes the same announcement sound like a burden or a dubious reward; B hears the reservation.
version_2.correct_next_move: Ask what is wrong with the arrangement before congratulating A.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: They picked me for team lead [dry].

items.title: The open goal
items.contrast: A comic retelling of a missed chance versus a loss that A is still taking hard.
items.cost_of_misread: Laughing at the second reading makes A feel blamed by a teammate when they already feel responsible. Consoling the first as if it were devastating refuses the bonding story.

version_1.label: A replay-worthy blunder
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A laughs first to make the miss available for team humor, and B joins without cruelty.
version_1.correct_next_move: Riff briefly on the absurd miss, then move on with the team.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I had an open goal and hit the post [chuckles].

version_2.label: Still raw after the miss
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh is an attempt not to show how badly the miss hurts; B's gentle tone declines to make it a team joke.
version_2.correct_next_move: Acknowledge the disappointment and reassure A that one play is not the whole match.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I had an open goal and hit the post [nervous laugh].

items.title: The flooded basement
items.setting: A phone call after a household emergency
items.contrast: A playful exaggeration about temporary inconvenience versus a real, self-softened plea for somewhere to stay.
items.cost_of_misread: If the parent treats the second version as a gag, the child may end the call without safe housing. If the parent responds to the first like an emergency placement, the child feels needlessly managed.

version_1.label: Joking about a temporary disruption
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's laugh makes moving in sound like comic exaggeration, and B playfully accepts the premise.
version_1.correct_next_move: Banter about the imagined arrangement, then casually ask what A's actual plan is.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: My basement flooded, so I guess I live with you now [laughs].

version_2.label: A real request hidden in humor
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh cushions a genuine need; B's gentle version of the same words is a concrete welcome rather than a joke.
version_2.correct_next_move: Say clearly that A can stay, and ask what needs to be brought over.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: My basement flooded, so I guess I live with you now [nervous laugh].

items.title: Coffee on the coat
items.relationship: Strangers who need to be careful with each other
items.contrast: Permission to share a tiny accident joke versus polite covering for a real inconvenience.
items.cost_of_misread: If A joins the second version as though the coat owner is amused, A dodges responsibility and leaves B with a stained coat. If A treats the first as anger, A makes B's generous release awkward.

version_1.label: The spill is genuinely brushed off
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: B's laugh releases A from the accident and permits a small, mutual joke.
version_1.correct_next_move: Offer an apology, accept the release, and keep any joke very brief.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I got coffee on your coat [wincing].

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's fine. It was already wet [laughs].

version_2.label: Polite words, real annoyance
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: B's strained laugh says "it's fine" without actually making it fine; A's nervous answer should lead into repair, not a joke.
version_2.correct_next_move: Apologize again and offer to pay for cleaning or replace the coat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I got coffee on your coat [wincing].

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's fine. It was already wet [strained].

items.title: The ex at the party
items.contrast: Bonding over an absurd coincidence versus signaling a need to get out of an uncomfortable situation.
items.cost_of_misread: Treating the second as entertainment can trap A near someone they are trying to avoid. Treating the first as a crisis makes a silly coincidence heavy and controlling.

version_1.label: A ridiculous party coincidence
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's laugh offers the ex's presence as another absurd detail of a strange party, and B joins the bit.
version_1.correct_next_move: Make a light joke and follow A's lead about whether to stay.

version_2.label: An exit signal
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh masks discomfort; B's gentle response treats the same coincidence as a cue to check whether A wants support.
version_2.correct_next_move: Offer to leave, switch rooms, or stay beside A without making the ex into entertainment.

items.title: The moved surgery
items.setting: A family call about a hospitalized parent
items.contrast: Bonding through dark humor about repeated scheduling chaos versus using humor to avoid falling apart.
items.cost_of_misread: A joke in the second reading trivializes a frightening family situation and leaves A alone with it. Solemn reassurance in the first can shut down the small bit of relief A is trying to create.

version_1.label: Dark humor as family bonding
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's chuckle invites B to mock the absurd scheduling, creating a moment of relief together.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the restrained dark humor, then check on practical details.

version_2.label: Overwhelmed behind composure
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's strained delivery is not an invitation to joke; B's gentle line names the situation without pretending it is funny.
version_2.correct_next_move: Ask how A is holding up and offer specific help with calls, rides, or food.

items.title: The surprisingly clear report
items.contrast: Proud acceptance of an awkward compliment versus hurt at a backhanded compliment.
items.cost_of_misread: If B celebrates the second version without noticing the insult, B validates the manager's low expectations. If B treats the first as a slight, B undercuts A's real pride.

version_1.label: Awkward praise, happily received
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's delighted laugh treats the manager's clumsy wording as real recognition, and B shares the win.
version_1.correct_next_move: Congratulate A and affirm that the report was good work.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: "Surprisingly clear," she said about my report [delighted].

version_2.label: A backhanded compliment
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's dry laugh marks the quote as patronizing; B's gentle delivery recognizes the sting behind the nominal praise.
version_2.correct_next_move: Name the wording as backhanded and validate why it landed badly.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: "Surprisingly clear," she said about my report [dry].
